sections.html:
Green sits in the southeast corner of Summit County, between Akron and Canton. It covers 32.03 square miles of land plus 1.5 square miles of water, which is a lot of ground for a suburb. Expect subdivisions, lakeside lots and former farm parcels instead of a tight street grid. About 27,553 people live here, and 75.1 percent of households own their home.

Green uses ZIP codes 44232, 44312, 44319, 44685 and 44216, and some of those addresses are shared with neighboring places. Before you rely on any city rule, ask the Summit County Fiscal Office to confirm your parcel is inside the city limits. In a listing, name both the city and Green Local Schools, since many Green addresses carry Akron-area ZIP codes.

Interstate 77 serves the city, and the Akron-Canton Regional Airport lies partly inside Green. Buyers also look at Boettler Park, a 26-acre park with trails and fishing, and the Singer Lake Bog nature preserve.

The middle owned home is valued at $280,200 and the middle household earns $95,047. Owners dominate, so most of your competition on a listing is other owner-occupied houses, with 5.3 percent of the 11,825 housing units vacant at the last full count. The city has grown at every count, from 22,817 residents in 2000 to 27,475 in 2020.

The city's Zoning Division issues permits, inspects new structures and enforces the City Code. It also takes right-of-way applications for aprons and road openings. Its Zoning page lists the most common code complaints:

  • High grass
  • Litter, garbage and debris
  • Junk or inoperable vehicles
  • Storage of RVs, campers and boats
  • Property disrepair

Clear any of these before you list. The division is at the Central Administration Building, 1755 Town Park Blvd., and the phone is 330-896-6605. Call to ask whether your address has an open complaint. The Land Development Code is in Part Twelve of the city's codified ordinances.

For building permits and inspections, the city also points to the Summit County Department of Building Standards in Akron. Summit County Public Health on West Market Street handles health permits. If the lot has a septic system, ask Public Health what records it holds, because a buyer will ask.

sections.h2: What does the Summit County Fiscal Office charge to transfer a Green deed?
sections.html:
The county's conveyance fee is $4.00 per $1,000 of the price, rounded up to the next $100. The office adds 50 cents for each lot in the legal description, even on exempt transfers. For comparison, Hancock and Franklin counties show $3 per $1,000.

On the Property Transfer page, the department takes the DTE 100 statement of value, or the DTE 100(EX) form when an exemption applies, under ORC 319.202 and 319.54(G)(3). Properly prepared forms must reach the Property Transfer Department by 3:30 p.m. for same-day approval of the legal description.

The value on the statement is the full consideration, and that includes any mortgage or lien balance the buyer takes on. The grantor pays the fee, and willfully falsifying the value is prohibited.

The Recording Division is at 175 South Main Street, 4th floor, Akron. Ohio law (ORC 5301.25) sends every deed to the county recorder, and the reason is practical: an unrecorded deed loses to a later buyer who had no notice of it. Ask the Recording Division for the current per-page recording charge.

One drafting rule catches people. When a survey was made of the land being conveyed, the surveyor's name has to appear in the deed, and the county auditor can insist on it. If you have a survey from your purchase, hand it to the title company early so the description is drafted right the first time. A seller who skips this step can see closing slip a few days while the deed is redrafted.

Most sellers never carry the deed in. A title company or closing agent normally prepares it, files the transfer forms and pays the fees from your proceeds.

Green fought the NEXUS Pipeline in court starting in 2016 because the line runs near residential neighborhoods, wetlands and the Comet Lake Dam. Construction began in 2018 after the city reached a $7.5 million settlement. If your lot is near the route, check your title paperwork for any easement before a buyer asks.

From about 1950, farmers began selling land to developers, so Green houses range from older farm properties to newer subdivision homes. An older house with an original well, septic system or outbuildings will draw different questions from an inspector than a recent subdivision home.

sections.h2: Which sale route works for a Green house on a deadline?
sections.html:
• Agent listing: a fit for move-in-ready homes where recent nearby sales give a clear price.
  • Investor sale: suited to dated houses, open code complaints, or an estate sale on a deadline.
  • Owner sale: saves commission but requires you to prepare the DTE 100 and deed paperwork.
  • Sale to a relative or neighbor: the exemption form may apply, and the 50 cent lot fee is owed either way.

Whichever route you pick, price the house against nearby Green sales and check for open zoning complaints.

A cash sale skips the weeks of showings and lender appraisal, but the paperwork is the same, so it helps to know the order.

  1. Confirm the parcel is inside Green and note the school district.
  2. Call the Zoning Division about open complaints and fix the visible ones.
  3. Gather the survey and title papers, plus any septic records.
  4. Choose a route and compare each written offer by what you would keep after repairs and holding costs.
  5. Have the title company prepare the deed and the DTE 100, with the full consideration stated.
  6. Pay the conveyance fee and the 50 cent lot charge at closing, and let the Recording Division file the deed.

If the buyer is a relative, ask the Fiscal Office whether the DTE 100(EX) exemption form applies before closing day.

Bring a few things to the title company: a photo ID, the survey if you have one, any easement or septic papers, and the loan payoff details if a mortgage remains. The mortgage or lien balance is paid from your proceeds at closing, and the buyer's side confirms the numbers on the statement of value match the contract.

faqs.q: Who issues permits for a house in Green?
faqs.a: The city's Zoning Division handles zoning permits and inspections of new structures. The Summit County Department of Building Standards is the county agency for building permits.

faqs.q: How much is the Summit County conveyance fee on a Green sale?
faqs.a: The fee is $4.00 per $1,000, with the price rounded up to the next $100, plus 50 cents per lot. Forms in by 3:30 p.m. get same-day legal description approval.

faqs.q: Where does a Green deed get recorded?
faqs.a: In Akron, at the Fiscal Office Recording Division on South Main Street. Ohio records a deed in the county where the land sits.

faqs.q: Is my Green house inside the city limits?
faqs.a: Not always, since some ZIP codes are shared with neighboring places. Ask the Summit County Fiscal Office to confirm your parcel.

faqs.q: How do I find out about code complaints on my Green house?
faqs.a: Call the Zoning Division at 330-896-6605. Overgrown grass, junk vehicles, stored RVs and general disrepair top its list of violations.
